title: Choose the inspection workspace
question: This is a completely fresh direction set for the multi-run inspection console.

options.label: Corridor Command Map
options.lineage: transport control maps, work-zone boards, route diagrams
options.thesis: Every inspection is a live point on an infrastructure corridor, with its evidence and decisions unfolding beside the network.
options.viewport: A slim run command rail feeds a horizontal workflow route; the selected run opens below into dedicated evidence, RAG, plan, schedule, and report views.
options.risk: The route metaphor must stay secondary to the actual data or it can become decorative.

options.label: Inspection Signal Bench
options.lineage: oscilloscopes, trigger controls, persistent signal traces
options.thesis: The workflow is a live diagnostic signal that locks into a durable case once every stage has stabilized.
options.viewport: A compact run selector and stage trace occupy the top, while the chosen case fills a bright technical reading surface below.
options.risk: Audience identification is moderate, but live progress and crash recovery become exceptionally clear.
options.case: Best for runtime visibility; formal report review needs a deliberately calmer reading layer.

options.label: Deployable Case Sheet
options.lineage: Miura-fold engineering sheets and aerospace specifications
options.thesis: A run begins as a compact record and unfolds into linked evidence, retrieval, planning, schedule, and report regions.
options.viewport: The selected run unfolds across a diagonal technical grid while the run list remains compressed at the edge.
options.risk: The folding structure can complicate responsive behavior and repeated operational scanning.
options.case: Strong relationship mapping; weaker for frequent switching among many runs.

options.label: Signal Grid
options.lineage: man-machine diagrams, traffic signals, wiring schematics
options.thesis: Agents, tools, and decisions form one visible circuit whose active path lights as each inspection advances.
options.viewport: A strict agent-and-tool grid occupies the center, with the selected run's result views attached as numbered destinations.
options.risk: The workflow topology is memorable but may overemphasize implementation details for ordinary operators.
options.case: Excellent agent traceability; weaker focus on inspection evidence itself.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional admin dashboard with sidebar navigation, metric cards, and stacked result panels.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar dashboard shell with intake form, run table, and detail cards.
